reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational concept of 'fundamental drives' unifies physiological need and learned behavioral patterns into a single motivational framework. This is mathematically modeled as D + S, where D represents innate physiological demands and S denotes sign-gestalt readiness. The dualism of appetites and aversions emerges as a partitioning of these drives into positive and negative motivational poles. Each pole exhibits three constitutive phases—initiating, sustaining, and terminating—which can be formalized as time-dependent dynamical systems. The core gestalt readiness remains invariant under learning, suggesting a fixed kernel within a flexible envelope. This structure supports both Bayesian inference in GSI (where D and S inform prior beliefs) and state-transition logic in GSE (where appetitive/aversive states guide action selection). The system's robustness depends on maintaining separation between innate core and learned modification, with breakdown occurring when learning destabilizes core readiness.
